chunks: My father (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya ibn Imran al-Ash'ari, from Hamdan ibn Sulayman, from Ayyub ibn Nuh, from Isma'il al-Farra', from a man, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him):

Did the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) not say regarding Abu Dharr (may Allah have mercy on him): 'The green shade (sky) has not shadowed, nor the dry earth (ground) have carried, anyone with a tongue more truthful than Abu Dharr'? He said: 'Yes.' I said: 'Then what about the Messenger of Allah and the Commander of the Faithful? And what about al-Hasan and al-Husayn?' He said to me: 'How many months are in a year?' I said: 'Twelve months.' He said: 'How many of them are sacred?' I said: 'Four months.' He said: 'Is the month of Ramadan among them?' I said: 'No.' He said: 'Indeed, in the month of Ramadan there is a night that is better than a thousand months. Indeed, we are the Ahl al-Bayt, and no one is comparable to us.'

key_terms.أَبُو ذَرٍّ: Abu Dharr (a prominent companion known for truthfulness)
key_terms.أَهْلُ بَيْتٍ: Ahl al-Bayt (the Household of the Prophet)
key_terms.لَيْلَةُ الْقَدْرِ: The Night of Decree (implied by 'a night better than a thousand months)'

ai.seo_question: How does the Imam explain the unique status of the Ahl al-Bayt compared to other virtuous companions like Abu Dharr?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq records this dialogue to clarify the theological nuance between the general truthfulness of Abu Dharr al-Ghifari and the unique, intrinsic superiority of the Ahl al-Bayt. The Imam employs the analogy of Laylat al-Qadr within Ramadan to illustrate that while others may possess high virtue, the Ahl al-Bayt possess a distinct, incomparable status ('la nuqasu bih') that transcends simple quantitative comparison.
